_what: PolicyEngine's PUBLISHED estimate of the same reform, kept as a history row on the CenTax claims so the published miss stays on the page. Read from the dashboard's own results file; nothing here is recomputed.
commit_note: main on 2026-10-21 (Merge pull request #6, 2026-10-12); the live page builds from main

reform.basis: src/childcare_100k/config.py at f25f0db (REFORM_PARAMETERS, parameter_changes: each limit set to infinity in every analysis year)

corrections: Six local corrections applied to every run, baseline and reform alike (src/childcare_100k/corrections.py at f25f0db): exactly £100,000 qualifies; a partner on a specified benefit need not pass the minimum earnings test; the universal and targeted 15 hours are a floor that eligibility for the extended hours never removes (policyengine-uk#1930); salary sacrifice returned to pay from April 2029 is not income for the limits; Tax-Free Childcare regards a partner on a caring or incapacity benefit as in qualifying paid work; both schemes test the claimant and partner.
fiscal_year_rule: src/childcare_100k/config.py at f25f0db: 'Fiscal years named by start year ("2026" = 2026-27).'

values_gbp_bn.field: budget.gross_bn.thirty_hours (the 30-hours leg: extended, universal and targeted entitlements; budget.thirty_hours_components_bn puts it all in extended)

hours_draw: microcosm#1126 (closed 2026-10-16) reports that this release draws maximum_extended_childcare_hours_usage ~ clip(N(15.019, 4.972), 0, 30), a mean of about 15 of the 30 weekly hours, and derives DfE's mean as about 28.5 hours: https://github.com/PolicyEngine/microcosm/issues/1126
